# GBx Co-Chair Alastair Paterson on his $160M exit, and starting over with Harmonic

---

Alastair Paterson co-founded Digital Shadows in 2011, scaled it to 500 customers across four continents, and sold it for $160 million in 2022. But this isn’t a story about a founder riding into the sunset after a successful exit. Alastair did the opposite and put himself back in the founder seat, building Harmonic Security. He is also the driving force behind the UK Cyber Flywheel and has recently been appointed as Co-Chair of the GBx Board. In this GBx Founder Spotlight, he shares what keeps driving him forward and why British founders need to move more quickly.

Not many people build a company from zero to acquisition. Fewer still walk away from a successful exit and willingly start the clock again and build from scratch. Alastair Paterson is one of them.

Alastair co-founded Digital Shadows in 2011 and led it to become an internationally recognised leader in threat intelligence and digital risk protection, before its acquisition by ReliaQuest for $160 million in July 2022. He took a breath, briefly, and then did it all again, building Harmonic Security, enabling enterprises to adopt generative AI without putting their sensitive data at risk.

## 2006-07 Alastair Paterson

Alastair Paterson is an inspirational Rotary leader and enjoys the whole-hearted support of all Rotarians in Grand Cayman and of his family (Meg, his wife, and daughters : Emma and Penny). His major accomplishments in Rotary since he first joined in 1984 are : - Assistant Governor for the Cayman Islands (2003-2004 during which time Alastair organised the very successful Family of Rotary conference attended by all 3 Grand Cayman clubs; - Charter President of the Rotary Club of Grand Cayman Sunrise - 2002 / 2003, during which time membership increased from 34 to 64; - President of the Rotary Club of Grand Cayman - 1996 / 1997, during which time membership increased by 20%, over the 100 mark for the first time; - Eight times a Paul Harris Fellow; - District Conference chairman for PDG Richard Harris in 1993; - Board member of Rotary clubs for over 10 years with responsibilities ranging from fund raising, sergeant and fellowship to community, vocational and international service. - Started Cayman HospiceCare in 1997; - and Vice chairman of the Pines Retirement Home. Alastair Paterson is also property consultant with special expertise in development managementn financial and contract management and valuations. Commercial and resort residential are his two areas of main speciality.

Alastair Paterson Is Making Sure the AI Revolution Doesn't Come at the Cost of Company Data

# Alastair Paterson Is Making Sure the AI Revolution Doesn't Come at the Cost of Company Data

 

Enterprises are racing to adopt AI, but the path is largely unsecured. Forbes Technology Council member Alastair Paterson, CEO and co-founder of Harmonic Security, has spent his career watching companies leak data they didn't know was leaving. Now, he's built a platform designed to make sure AI doesn't make that problem catastrophically worse.

Paterson has seen this movie before. The tools change, the urgency escalates, and somewhere in the rush to stay competitive, a company exposes data it can't get back. He spent more than a decade at Digital Shadows watching that pattern play out at enterprise scale before selling the company to ReliaQuest for $160 million in 2022.

## From Threat Intelligence to the AI Governance Gap

Digital Shadows gave Paterson a front-row seat to how companies lose data. Not always through sophisticated attacks, but through carelessness, speed, and the gap between what IT departments approve and what employees actually use.

"In 2011, I co-founded Digital Shadows," Paterson explains. "We learned about the sheer volume of data companies can leak out of their businesses — whether accidentally or via threat actors. AI has exacerbated all of this."

# One thing the US does better than the UK is the culture of forward-leaning, early-adopter CISOs. They are active on advisory boards and act as design partners at the early stage. This … | Alastair Paterson · LinkedIn · 2025-10-06

**Alastair Paterson**: Chief Executive Officer at Harmonic Security for 3 years with 3 years 2 months of total professional experience. Based in San Francisco, California, United States [US].

---

One thing the US does better than the UK is the culture of forward-leaning, early-adopter CISOs. They are active on advisory boards and act as design partners at the early stage. This has huge benefits for their business and the startup ecosystem more generally.

In the UK, those people exist but are less common. UK cyber startups often find their design partners in the US rather than closer to home. But it doesn't have to be this way!

For this panel, we have gathered some of the top UK CISOs who do this well, and will share their experiences + thoughts on how to navigate this:

[Kirsty Kelly](https://linkedin.com/in/kirsty-l-kelly) (CFC)
[Simon Goldsmith](https://linkedin.com/in/smg-cyber) (OVO)
Mark Sutton (Bain Capital)
[Munawar V.](https://linkedin.com/in/munawar-v-b636802) (Close Brothers)

Are you a CISO in the UK would like to find out more? Join us this week: https://lnkd.in/dZVim-y7
